text:
Alex Chen: Quick heads-up — Acme workshop Tue AM. They pushed hard for reliable JSON output + a clear fallback when the model drifts. Need a product decision on mode + launch bar.
Maya Patel: Where does this sit in the current roadmap? We merged json-mode planning but didn't finalize strict vs repair behavior.
Luis Ortega: From CS: Acme expects schema enforcement and an automated retry/fallback path. Their ask: <1% invalid responses in production, but they can accept repair attempts if we document latency/cost impact.
Samir Gupta: Runtime POV: strict enforcement (reject on validation fail) is simpler but will bubble errors to customers. Repair (attempt to autocorrect) adds extra model calls and latency + complexity in the validator/repair heuristics.
Emily Rivera: Implementation proposal — pipeline model:

```
json_mode:
  strictness: "repair"    # options: strict | repair | soft
  validator:
    schema_support: [json-schema-draft7, refs-readonly]
    max_repair_attempts: 1
  retry_policy:
    attempts: 2
    on: [validation_error, parse_error]
  fallback_order: [tool_call, text_mode]
```

Flow: model->validate -> if fail attempt repair heuristics -> if still fail retry with model-variant (smaller/larger context) -> if still fail call a special tool or return text-mode with structured hint.
Alex Chen: For SLA/canary propose targets: canary pass >=95% direct valid JSON, post-repair valid >=99%, p50 added latency budget <= +80ms, p95 <= +200ms. Also capture cost delta on error paths. Thoughts?
Maya Patel: Acme said 99% post-repair is acceptable. We need explicit acceptance criteria + console telemetry (per-prompt validation status, repair trace, cost increment). Also they'd like function/tool-calling as an escape hatch for critical fields.
Samir Gupta: Note on cost: repair+retry will increase token usage on failure routes ~20-40% depending on attempts. We must surface token-level breakdown and gating thresholds before GA.
Emily Rivera: Agree. We'll expose these knobs via the API and Console and add debug flags for canary. Example API shape:

```
POST /v1/generate
{
  "model":"rw-infer-1",
  "json_mode": { "strictness": "repair", "retry_policy": {"attempts":2}},
  "schema": "{...}",
  "prompt": "..."
}
```

We will emit structured telemetry: validation_status, repairs_attempted, fallback_taken, token_delta.
Alex Chen: Action items — Samir: perf + cost estimate by EOD Thu; Emily: draft API schema + examples for docs; Maya: confirm acceptance criteria with Acme and capture UAT prompts; Luis: schedule the workshop and set expectations with Acme. @launch-bot please create a checklist.
launch-bot: Checklist created: /launch/structured-output-acme — owners assigned. :white_check_mark:
Maya Patel: One more scope item: support JSON Schema $ref and arrays for their embedding->rerank pipeline. They pass large arrays of scored items.
Samir Gupta: We can support readonly $ref resolution in v1 (validate references that are inline or provided), but full remote $ref resolution or recursive schema transforms should be post-canary.
Alex Chen: Decision: proceed to canary with default repair-on, but customer can opt into strict mode. Monitor costs/latency closely and hard-stop if p95 latency cost exceeds thresholds. Any objections?
Emily Rivera: :thumbsup: I'll prototype the validator + repair loop next week and mock metrics.
Luis Ortega: Acme confirmed they're willing to be a canary customer and will provide evaluation prompts and failure examples.
Maya Patel: :eyes: Good. I'll own UAT metrics and will sync results back here. If anyone hits blockers, ping me or Alex.
